title: CRS licence to manufacture Mobile Phones in India
heading: CRS licence to manufacture Mobile Phones in India
excerpt: What licence and certification a factory needs before it can manufacture Mobile Phones (IS 13252 (Part 1)) for sale in India.
body: Mobile Phones sits on the BIS Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS / Scheme II) against IS 13252 (Part 1). HSN 85171300. Mandatory (CRS Registration). This is a lab-test registration of the brand and model — not a Scheme I ISI factory licence — and you still need it if the finished goods are made in India.

To manufacture Mobile Phones in India you typically hold GST, a factory or Udyam record, and then file CRS on the BIS portal with the IS 13252 (Part 1) test report from a recognised lab. You do not wait for a factory inspection the way ISI Scheme I works. The registration number and the BIS Standard Mark go on the product, packaging or rating plate before you stock or sell.

Listed laboratory charges for IS 13252 (Part 1) run ₹25,000–₹1,95,000 excluding GST. Keep the BOM, enclosure, PSU and critical insulation identical to the tested sample — a board spin or adapter swap is a new model and a new CRS line. If the Mobile Phones SKU carries Wi-Fi, Bluetooth or a cellular radio, stack a WPC ETA / equipment type approval on the same project — CRS never replaces the radio licence.
If the listed test price looks expensive, contact Certko — we regularly secure up to 30% lesser pricing on Mobile Phones CRS testing and handle the portal filing so the factory can keep building.

title: Importing Mobile Phones from China: CRS registration
heading: Importing Mobile Phones from China: CRS registration
excerpt: A finished Mobile Phones made in China cannot be sold in India on a CCC mark. Map IS 13252 (Part 1) CRS before the shipment leaves.
body: Chinese factories often already hold CCC, SRRC or a CB report for Mobile Phones. None of those marks let you sell the goods in India. For HSN 85171300 the Indian gate is BIS CRS against IS 13252 (Part 1). Mandatory (CRS Registration).

The Chinese manufacturer can own the CRS registration and appoint an Authorised Indian Representative (AIR), or the Indian importer can register the brand it places on the market. Customs officers check the CRS number on Mobile Phones consignments — a missing number is a hold, not a “pay later” option.

Plan 6–10 weeks for testing plus portal queries. Listed charges ₹25,000–₹1,95,000. Do not assume a Shenzhen CB report converts automatically — Indian national differences and the current IS 13252 (Part 1) edition still have to match. If the Mobile Phones SKU carries Wi-Fi, Bluetooth or a cellular radio, stack a WPC ETA / equipment type approval on the same project — CRS never replaces the radio licence.
Certko maps the China construction to IS 13252 (Part 1), books the lab, and files CRS so the first container is not the test sample.

title: Importing Mobile Phones from Vietnam: CRS registration
heading: Importing Mobile Phones from Vietnam: CRS registration
excerpt: Vietnam-built Mobile Phones still needs Indian CRS on IS 13252 (Part 1) before it can be sold here — CR or ASEAN marks are not enough.
body: A growing share of Mobile Phones now ships from Vietnam instead of China. MIC / CR marks and an ASEAN CB route help other markets. They do not replace BIS CRS for India. The standard remains IS 13252 (Part 1), HSN 85171300. Mandatory (CRS Registration).

Treat the Vietnamese plant as a foreign manufacturer: appoint an AIR if the brand owner sits outside India, test the Vietnam-built sample (not a leftover China unit), and register that construction. A China CRS line does not cover a Vietnam second source unless the BOM and layout are proven identical and BIS accepts the series.

Listed testing for this SKU is ₹25,000–₹1,95,000. If you dual-source China and Vietnam, budget two sample sets and say so on the portal — mixed constructions are the usual query that stalls Mobile Phones registrations. If the Mobile Phones SKU carries Wi-Fi, Bluetooth or a cellular radio, stack a WPC ETA / equipment type approval on the same project — CRS never replaces the radio licence.
Certko files the Vietnam plant as its own manufacturing location on CRS and keeps the China line separate so neither factory blocks the other.

title: Assemble Mobile Phones in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
heading: Assemble Mobile Phones in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
excerpt: Importing spare parts or CKD/SKD kits and assembling Mobile Phones in India does not dodge BIS. You can always take the CRS route on the finished unit.
body: If you import spare parts, SKD or CKD kits of Mobile Phones from China or Vietnam and want to assemble in India, you can always go for the CRS route. BIS looks at the finished product you place on the Indian market — Mobile Phones under IS 13252 (Part 1) — not at each screw and bare PCB in the inbound carton.

Unpopulated housings, displays, batteries shipped as parts, or a CKD kit billed as components usually stay outside CRS at the border. The moment your Indian line assembles a complete, usable Mobile Phones (HSN 85171300 as a finished good), CRS registration is what lets you manufacture and sell it. That is often cleaner than importing a CBU and fighting a finished-goods hold.

Register the Indian assembly site as the manufacturer. Test the unit that actually comes off the Indian line — not a golden sample from Shenzhen — against IS 13252 (Part 1). Lab window 6–10 weeks, listed charges ₹25,000–₹1,95,000. Keep a parts-trace file so a Vietnam substitute cell or adapter does not silently break the registered construction. If the Mobile Phones SKU carries Wi-Fi, Bluetooth or a cellular radio, stack a WPC ETA / equipment type approval on the same project — CRS never replaces the radio licence.

This is the route Certko recommends when a brand wants Indian value-add: import parts, assemble here, test the Indian build, file CRS. One registration covers the manufactured goods. Contact Certko if you want the parts list and the finished-goods HSN scoped before the first kit lands.

title: CKD, SKD or CBU for Mobile Phones — CRS still applies
heading: CKD, SKD or CBU for Mobile Phones — CRS still applies
excerpt: Knocked-down kits of Mobile Phones do not skip BIS. Choose the import form, then register the finished goods on CRS.
body: Brands argue CBU versus CKD to cut duty on Mobile Phones. That is a customs conversation. The compliance conversation is simpler: whatever form you import, the finished Mobile Phones sold in India needs CRS on IS 13252 (Part 1) (HSN 85171300).

CBU: register before you sell, and usually before you promise a delivery date, because a finished electronic good is easy for customs to query. CKD/SKD: import parts, assemble in India, and take the CRS manufacturer route on the Indian-built unit. Spare parts sold as parts stay out of CRS until they become a complete Mobile Phones.

You can always go for the assembly-plus-CRS route when the commercial plan is Indian value-add. Test the unit that leaves the Indian line. 6–10 weeks, listed charges ₹25,000–₹1,95,000. If the Mobile Phones SKU carries Wi-Fi, Bluetooth or a cellular radio, stack a WPC ETA / equipment type approval on the same project — CRS never replaces the radio licence.
Certko will tell you which cartons are parts and which are Mobile Phones before you file the Bill of Entry, then run the CRS filing that matches that choice.

title: Assemble Servers in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route

BIS looks at the finished product you place on the Indian market — Servers under IS 13252 (Part 1) — not at each screw and bare PCB in the inbound carton.

Unpopulated housings, displays, batteries shipped as parts, or a CKD kit billed as components usually stay outside CRS at the border. The moment your Indian line assembles a complete, usable Servers (HSN 84714190 as a finished good), CRS registration is what lets you manufacture and sell it. title: CKD, SKD or CBU for Wireless Keyboards — CRS still applies
heading: CKD, SKD or CBU for Wireless Keyboards — CRS still applies
excerpt: Knocked-down kits of Wireless Keyboards do not skip BIS. Choose the import form, then register the finished goods on CRS.
body: Brands argue CBU versus CKD to cut duty on Wireless Keyboards. That is a customs conversation. The compliance conversation is simpler: whatever form you import, the finished Wireless Keyboards sold in India needs CRS on IS 13252 (Part 1) (HSN 84716060).

CBU: register before you sell, and usually before you promise a delivery date, because a finished electronic good is easy for customs to query. CKD/SKD: import parts, assemble in India, and take the CRS manufacturer route on the Indian-built unit. Spare parts sold as parts stay out of CRS until they become a complete Wireless Keyboards.

You can always go for the assembly-plus-CRS route when the commercial plan is Indian value-add. Test the unit that leaves the Indian line. 6–10 weeks, listed charges ₹25,000–₹1,95,000. title: CRS licence to manufacture Point of Sale Terminals in India
heading: CRS licence to manufacture Point of Sale Terminals in India
excerpt: What licence and certification a factory needs before it can manufacture Point of Sale Terminals (IS 13252 (Part 1)) for sale in India.
body: Point of Sale Terminals sits on the BIS Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS / Scheme II) against IS 13252 (Part 1). HSN 84705010. Mandatory (CRS Registration). This is a lab-test registration of the brand and model — not a Scheme I ISI factory licence — and you still need it if the finished goods are made in India.

To manufacture Point of Sale Terminals in India you typically hold GST, a factory or Udyam record, and then file CRS on the BIS portal with the IS 13252 (Part 1) test report from a recognised lab. You do not wait for a factory inspection the way ISI Scheme I works. The registration number and the BIS Standard Mark go on the product, packaging or rating plate before you stock or sell.

Listed laboratory charges for IS 13252 (Part 1) run ₹25,000–₹1,95,000 excluding GST. Keep the BOM, enclosure, PSU and critical insulation identical to the tested sample — a board spin or adapter swap is a new model and a new CRS line.

If the listed test price looks expensive, contact Certko — we regularly secure up to 30% lesser pricing on Point of Sale Terminals CRS testing and handle the portal filing so the factory can keep building.

title: Importing Point of Sale Terminals from Vietnam: CRS registration
heading: Importing Point of Sale Terminals from Vietnam: CRS registration
excerpt: Vietnam-built Point of Sale Terminals still needs Indian CRS on IS 13252 (Part 1) before it can be sold here — CR or ASEAN marks are not enough.
body: A growing share of Point of Sale Terminals now ships from Vietnam instead of China. MIC / CR marks and an ASEAN CB route help other markets. They do not replace BIS CRS for India. The standard remains IS 13252 (Part 1), HSN 84705010. Mandatory (CRS Registration).

Treat the Vietnamese plant as a foreign manufacturer: appoint an AIR if the brand owner sits outside India, test the Vietnam-built sample (not a leftover China unit), and register that construction. A China CRS line does not cover a Vietnam second source unless the BOM and layout are proven identical and BIS accepts the series.

Listed testing for this SKU is ₹25,000–₹1,95,000. If you dual-source China and Vietnam, budget two sample sets and say so on the portal — mixed constructions are the usual query that stalls Point of Sale Terminals registrations.
Certko files the Vietnam plant as its own manufacturing location on CRS and keeps the China line separate so neither factory blocks the other.

title: Assemble Point of Sale Terminals in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
heading: Assemble Point of Sale Terminals in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
excerpt: Importing spare parts or CKD/SKD kits and assembling Point of Sale Terminals in India does not dodge BIS. You can always take the CRS route on the finished unit.
body: If you import spare parts, SKD or CKD kits of Point of Sale Terminals from China or Vietnam and want to assemble in India, you can always go for the CRS route. BIS looks at the finished product you place on the Indian market — Point of Sale Terminals under IS 13252 (Part 1) — not at each screw and bare PCB in the inbound carton.

Unpopulated housings, displays, batteries shipped as parts, or a CKD kit billed as components usually stay outside CRS at the border. The moment your Indian line assembles a complete, usable Point of Sale Terminals (HSN 84705010 as a finished good), CRS registration is what lets you manufacture and sell it. That is often cleaner than importing a CBU and fighting a finished-goods hold.

Register the Indian assembly site as the manufacturer. Test the unit that actually comes off the Indian line — not a golden sample from Shenzhen — against IS 13252 (Part 1). Lab window 6–10 weeks, listed charges ₹25,000–₹1,95,000. Keep a parts-trace file so a Vietnam substitute cell or adapter does not silently break the registered construction.

title: Assemble Printers & Plotters in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
heading: Assemble Printers & Plotters in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
excerpt: Importing spare parts or CKD/SKD kits and assembling Printers & Plotters in India does not dodge BIS. You can always take the CRS route on the finished unit.
body: If you import spare parts, SKD or CKD kits of Printers & Plotters from China or Vietnam and want to assemble in India, you can always go for the CRS route. BIS looks at the finished product you place on the Indian market — Printers & Plotters under IS 13252 (Part 1) — not at each screw and bare PCB in the inbound carton.

Unpopulated housings, displays, batteries shipped as parts, or a CKD kit billed as components usually stay outside CRS at the border. The moment your Indian line assembles a complete, usable Printers & Plotters (HSN 84433210 as a finished good), CRS registration is what lets you manufacture and sell it. That is often cleaner than importing a CBU and fighting a finished-goods hold.

Register the Indian assembly site as the manufacturer. Test the unit that actually comes off the Indian line — not a golden sample from Shenzhen — against IS 13252 (Part 1). Lab window 6–10 weeks, listed charges ₹25,000–₹1,95,000. Keep a parts-trace file so a Vietnam substitute cell or adapter does not silently break the registered construction.

title: CKD, SKD or CBU for Printers & Plotters — CRS still applies
heading: CKD, SKD or CBU for Printers & Plotters — CRS still applies

excerpt: Vietnam-built Automatic Data Processing Machines still needs Indian CRS on IS 13252 (Part 1) before it can be sold here — CR or ASEAN marks are not enough.

title: Assemble Automatic Data Processing Machines in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
heading: Assemble Automatic Data Processing Machines in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
excerpt: Importing spare parts or CKD/SKD kits and assembling Automatic Data Processing Machines in India does not dodge BIS. You can always take the CRS route on the finished unit.
body: If you import spare parts, SKD or CKD kits of Automatic Data Processing Machines from China or Vietnam and want to assemble in India, you can always go for the CRS route. BIS looks at the finished product you place on the Indian market — Automatic Data Processing Machines under IS 13252 (Part 1) — not at each screw and bare PCB in the inbound carton.

Unpopulated housings, displays, batteries shipped as parts, or a CKD kit billed as components usually stay outside CRS at the border. The moment your Indian line assembles a complete, usable Automatic Data Processing Machines (HSN 84714900 as a finished good), CRS registration is what lets you manufacture and sell it. That is often cleaner than importing a CBU and fighting a finished-goods hold.

Register the Indian assembly site as the manufacturer. Test the unit that actually comes off the Indian line — not a golden sample from Shenzhen — against IS 13252 (Part 1). Lab window 6–10 weeks, listed charges ₹25,000–₹1,95,000. Keep a parts-trace file so a Vietnam substitute cell or adapter does not silently break the registered construction.

title: Assemble Microwave Ovens in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
heading: Assemble Microwave Ovens in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
excerpt: Importing spare parts or CKD/SKD kits and assembling Microwave Ovens in India does not dodge BIS. You can always take the CRS route on the finished unit.
body: If you import spare parts, SKD or CKD kits of Microwave Ovens from China or Vietnam and want to assemble in India, you can always go for the CRS route. BIS looks at the finished product you place on the Indian market — Microwave Ovens under IS 302-2-25 — not at each screw and bare PCB in the inbound carton.

Unpopulated housings, displays, batteries shipped as parts, or a CKD kit billed as components usually stay outside CRS at the border. The moment your Indian line assembles a complete, usable Microwave Ovens (HSN 85165000 as a finished good), CRS registration is what lets you manufacture and sell it. That is often cleaner than importing a CBU and fighting a finished-goods hold.

Register the Indian assembly site as the manufacturer. Test the unit that actually comes off the Indian line — not a golden sample from Shenzhen — against IS 302-2-25. Lab window 6–10 weeks, listed charges ₹5,000–₹6,50,000. Keep a parts-trace file so a Vietnam substitute cell or adapter does not silently break the registered construction.

title: CKD, SKD or CBU for Microwave Ovens — CRS still applies
heading: CKD, SKD or CBU for Microwave Ovens — CRS still applies
excerpt: Knocked-down kits of Microwave Ovens do not skip BIS. Choose the import form, then register the finished goods on CRS.
body: Brands argue CBU versus CKD to cut duty on Microwave Ovens. That is a customs conversation. The compliance conversation is simpler: whatever form you import, the finished Microwave Ovens sold in India needs CRS on IS 302-2-25 (HSN 85165000).

CBU: register before you sell, and usually before you promise a delivery date, because a finished electronic good is easy for customs to query. CKD/SKD: import parts, assemble in India, and take the CRS manufacturer route on the Indian-built unit. Spare parts sold as parts stay out of CRS until they become a complete Microwave Ovens.
You can always go for the assembly-plus-CRS route when the commercial plan is Indian value-add. Test the unit that leaves the Indian line. 6–10 weeks, listed charges ₹5,000–₹6,50,000.
Certko will tell you which cartons are parts and which are Microwave Ovens before you file the Bill of Entry, then run the CRS filing that matches that choice.

title: CRS licence to manufacture Plasma / LCD / LED Televisions in India
heading: CRS licence to manufacture Plasma / LCD / LED Televisions in India
excerpt: What licence and certification a factory needs before it can manufacture Plasma / LCD / LED Televisions (IS 616) for sale in India.
body: Plasma / LCD / LED Televisions sits on the BIS Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS / Scheme II) against IS 616. HSN 85287217. Mandatory (CRS Registration). This is a lab-test registration of the brand and model — not a Scheme I ISI factory licence — and you still need it if the finished goods are made in India.

To manufacture Plasma / LCD / LED Televisions in India you typically hold GST, a factory or Udyam record, and then file CRS on the BIS portal with the IS 616 test report from a recognised lab. Unpopulated housings, displays, batteries shipped as parts, or a CKD kit billed as components usually stay outside CRS at the border. title: CKD, SKD or CBU for Electronic Musical Systems (>200W) — CRS still applies
heading: CKD, SKD or CBU for Electronic Musical Systems (>200W) — CRS still applies

CBU: register before you sell, and usually before you promise a delivery date, because a finished electronic good is easy for customs to query. title: CRS licence to manufacture Electronic Clocks with Mains Power in India
heading: CRS licence to manufacture Electronic Clocks with Mains Power in India
excerpt: What licence and certification a factory needs before it can manufacture Electronic Clocks with Mains Power (IS 302-2-26) for sale in India.
body: Electronic Clocks with Mains Power sits on the BIS Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS / Scheme II) against IS 302-2-26. HSN 91052100. Mandatory (CRS Registration). This is a lab-test registration of the brand and model — not a Scheme I ISI factory licence — and you still need it if the finished goods are made in India.

To manufacture Electronic Clocks with Mains Power in India you typically hold GST, a factory or Udyam record, and then file CRS on the BIS portal with the IS 302-2-26 test report from a recognised lab. title: Assemble Electronic Clocks with Mains Power in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
heading: Assemble Electronic Clocks with Mains Power in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
excerpt: Importing spare parts or CKD/SKD kits and assembling Electronic Clocks with Mains Power in India does not dodge BIS. You can always take the CRS route on the finished unit.
body: If you import spare parts, SKD or CKD kits of Electronic Clocks with Mains Power from China or Vietnam and want to assemble in India, you can always go for the CRS route. BIS looks at the finished product you place on the Indian market — Electronic Clocks with Mains Power under IS 302-2-26 — not at each screw and bare PCB in the inbound carton.

Unpopulated housings, displays, batteries shipped as parts, or a CKD kit billed as components usually stay outside CRS at the border. The moment your Indian line assembles a complete, usable Electronic Clocks with Mains Power (HSN 91052100 as a finished good), CRS registration is what lets you manufacture and sell it. That is often cleaner than importing a CBU and fighting a finished-goods hold.

Register the Indian assembly site as the manufacturer. Test the unit that actually comes off the Indian line — not a golden sample from Shenzhen — against IS 302-2-26. Lab window 6–10 weeks, listed charges ₹5,000–₹6,50,000. Keep a parts-trace file so a Vietnam substitute cell or adapter does not silently break the registered construction.

title: Assemble Adapters for IT Equipment in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
heading: Assemble Adapters for IT Equipment in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
excerpt: Importing spare parts or CKD/SKD kits and assembling Adapters for IT Equipment in India does not dodge BIS. You can always take the CRS route on the finished unit.
body: If you import spare parts, SKD or CKD kits of Adapters for IT Equipment from China or Vietnam and want to assemble in India, you can always go for the CRS route. BIS looks at the finished product you place on the Indian market — Adapters for IT Equipment under IS 13252 (Part 1) — not at each screw and bare PCB in the inbound carton.

Unpopulated housings, displays, batteries shipped as parts, or a CKD kit billed as components usually stay outside CRS at the border. The moment your Indian line assembles a complete, usable Adapters for IT Equipment (HSN 85044030 as a finished good), CRS registration is what lets you manufacture and sell it. That is often cleaner than importing a CBU and fighting a finished-goods hold.

Register the Indian assembly site as the manufacturer. Test the unit that actually comes off the Indian line — not a golden sample from Shenzhen — against IS 13252 (Part 1). Lab window 6–10 weeks, listed charges ₹25,000–₹1,95,000. Keep a parts-trace file so a Vietnam substitute cell or adapter does not silently break the registered construction.

heading: CKD, SKD or CBU for Adapters for IT Equipment — CRS still applies

title: CRS licence to manufacture Adapters for Audio/Video Equipment in India
heading: CRS licence to manufacture Adapters for Audio/Video Equipment in India
excerpt: What licence and certification a factory needs before it can manufacture Adapters for Audio/Video Equipment (IS 616) for sale in India.

This is a lab-test registration of the brand and model — not a Scheme I ISI factory licence — and you still need it if the finished goods are made in India.

BIS looks at the finished product you place on the Indian market — Power Banks for Portable Applications under IS 13252 (Part 1) / IS 16046 — not at each screw and bare PCB in the inbound carton.

Unpopulated housings, displays, batteries shipped as parts, or a CKD kit billed as components usually stay outside CRS at the border. title: Assemble Fixed General Purpose LED Luminaires in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
heading: Assemble Fixed General Purpose LED Luminaires in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
excerpt: Importing spare parts or CKD/SKD kits and assembling Fixed General Purpose LED Luminaires in India does not dodge BIS. You can always take the CRS route on the finished unit.
body: If you import spare parts, SKD or CKD kits of Fixed General Purpose LED Luminaires from China or Vietnam and want to assemble in India, you can always go for the CRS route. BIS looks at the finished product you place on the Indian market — Fixed General Purpose LED Luminaires under IS 10322 (Part 5/Sec 1) — not at each screw and bare PCB in the inbound carton.

Unpopulated housings, displays, batteries shipped as parts, or a CKD kit billed as components usually stay outside CRS at the border. The moment your Indian line assembles a complete, usable Fixed General Purpose LED Luminaires (HSN 94051100 as a finished good), CRS registration is what lets you manufacture and sell it. That is often cleaner than importing a CBU and fighting a finished-goods hold.

Register the Indian assembly site as the manufacturer. Test the unit that actually comes off the Indian line — not a golden sample from Shenzhen — against IS 10322 (Part 5/Sec 1). Lab window 6–10 weeks, listed charges ₹20,000–₹1,50,000. Keep a parts-trace file so a Vietnam substitute cell or adapter does not silently break the registered construction.

excerpt: Vietnam-built LED Luminaires for Road & Street Lighting still needs Indian CRS on IS 10322 (Part 5/Sec 3) before it can be sold here — CR or ASEAN marks are not enough.

Certko files the Vietnam plant as its own manufacturing location on CRS and keeps the China line separate so neither factory blocks the other.

title: Assemble LED Luminaires for Road & Street Lighting in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
heading: Assemble LED Luminaires for Road & Street Lighting in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
excerpt: Importing spare parts or CKD/SKD kits and assembling LED Luminaires for Road & Street Lighting in India does not dodge BIS. You can always take the CRS route on the finished unit.
body: If you import spare parts, SKD or CKD kits of LED Luminaires for Road & Street Lighting from China or Vietnam and want to assemble in India, you can always go for the CRS route. BIS looks at the finished product you place on the Indian market — LED Luminaires for Road & Street Lighting under IS 10322 (Part 5/Sec 3) — not at each screw and bare PCB in the inbound carton.

Unpopulated housings, displays, batteries shipped as parts, or a CKD kit billed as components usually stay outside CRS at the border. The moment your Indian line assembles a complete, usable LED Luminaires for Road & Street Lighting (HSN 94054090 as a finished good), CRS registration is what lets you manufacture and sell it. That is often cleaner than importing a CBU and fighting a finished-goods hold.

Register the Indian assembly site as the manufacturer. Test the unit that actually comes off the Indian line — not a golden sample from Shenzhen — against IS 10322 (Part 5/Sec 3). Lab window 6–10 weeks, listed charges ₹30,000–₹1,50,000. Keep a parts-trace file so a Vietnam substitute cell or adapter does not silently break the registered construction.

title: Assemble LED Hand Lamps in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
heading: Assemble LED Hand Lamps in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
excerpt: Importing spare parts or CKD/SKD kits and assembling LED Hand Lamps in India does not dodge BIS. You can always take the CRS route on the finished unit.

BIS looks at the finished product you place on the Indian market — LED Hand Lamps under IS 10322 (Part 5/Sec 6) — not at each screw and bare PCB in the inbound carton.

Unpopulated housings, displays, batteries shipped as parts, or a CKD kit billed as components usually stay outside CRS at the border. The moment your Indian line assembles a complete, usable LED Hand Lamps (HSN 94054090 as a finished good), CRS registration is what lets you manufacture and sell it. That is often cleaner than importing a CBU and fighting a finished-goods hold.

title: Assemble Recessed LED Luminaires in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
heading: Assemble Recessed LED Luminaires in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
excerpt: Importing spare parts or CKD/SKD kits and assembling Recessed LED Luminaires in India does not dodge BIS. You can always take the CRS route on the finished unit.
body: If you import spare parts, SKD or CKD kits of Recessed LED Luminaires from China or Vietnam and want to assemble in India, you can always go for the CRS route. BIS looks at the finished product you place on the Indian market — Recessed LED Luminaires under IS 10322 (Part 5/Sec 2) — not at each screw and bare PCB in the inbound carton.

Unpopulated housings, displays, batteries shipped as parts, or a CKD kit billed as components usually stay outside CRS at the border. The moment your Indian line assembles a complete, usable Recessed LED Luminaires (HSN 94051900 as a finished good), CRS registration is what lets you manufacture and sell it. That is often cleaner than importing a CBU and fighting a finished-goods hold.

Register the Indian assembly site as the manufacturer. Test the unit that actually comes off the Indian line — not a golden sample from Shenzhen — against IS 10322 (Part 5/Sec 2). Lab window 6–10 weeks, listed charges ₹20,000–₹1,50,000. Keep a parts-trace file so a Vietnam substitute cell or adapter does not silently break the registered construction.

excerpt: What a BIS-recognised lab will ask for when Bluetooth Speakers is tested to IS 616.
body: CRS evidence for Bluetooth Speakers is a complete IS 616 report from a BIS-recognised laboratory. Partial CE or FCC packets are useful background; they are not the CRS report. HSN 85182100.

Send the production-intent construction: the same enclosure, PSU, battery, display and insulation you will ship. Labs reject “engineering” boards that do not match the label drawing. Ask for a sample plan up front — Bluetooth Speakers often needs more than one unit if destructive clauses apply.

If the listed range looks wide, it is because clause packs and series testing differ. If the Bluetooth Speakers SKU carries Wi-Fi, Bluetooth or a cellular radio, stack a WPC ETA / equipment type approval on the same project — CRS never replaces the radio licence.
After the report, keep the sample seal photos and the critical-component list with the CRS file. A surveillance or series addition will ask for them.

title: Foreign factory and AIR duties for Bluetooth Speakers
heading: Foreign factory and AIR duties for Bluetooth Speakers

title: CKD, SKD or CBU for Bluetooth Speakers — CRS still applies
heading: CKD, SKD or CBU for Bluetooth Speakers — CRS still applies
excerpt: Knocked-down kits of Bluetooth Speakers do not skip BIS. Choose the import form, then register the finished goods on CRS.
body: Brands argue CBU versus CKD to cut duty on Bluetooth Speakers. That is a customs conversation. The compliance conversation is simpler: whatever form you import, the finished Bluetooth Speakers sold in India needs CRS on IS 616 (HSN 85182100).

CBU: register before you sell, and usually before you promise a delivery date, because a finished electronic good is easy for customs to query. CKD/SKD: import parts, assemble in India, and take the CRS manufacturer route on the Indian-built unit. Spare parts sold as parts stay out of CRS until they become a complete Bluetooth Speakers.

You can always go for the assembly-plus-CRS route when the commercial plan is Indian value-add. Test the unit that leaves the Indian line. 6–10 weeks, listed charges ₹1–₹1,80,000. If the Bluetooth Speakers SKU carries Wi-Fi, Bluetooth or a cellular radio, stack a WPC ETA / equipment type approval on the same project — CRS never replaces the radio licence.
Certko will tell you which cartons are parts and which are Bluetooth Speakers before you file the Bill of Entry, then run the CRS filing that matches that choice.

title: CRS licence to manufacture USB External Hard Disk Drives / SSDs in India
heading: CRS licence to manufacture USB External Hard Disk Drives / SSDs in India
excerpt: What licence and certification a factory needs before it can manufacture USB External Hard Disk Drives / SSDs (IS 13252 (Part 1)) for sale in India.
body: USB External Hard Disk Drives / SSDs sits on the BIS Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS / Scheme II) against IS 13252 (Part 1). HSN 84717020. Mandatory (CRS Registration). This is a lab-test registration of the brand and model — not a Scheme I ISI factory licence — and you still need it if the finished goods are made in India.

To manufacture USB External Hard Disk Drives / SSDs in India you typically hold GST, a factory or Udyam record, and then file CRS on the BIS portal with the IS 13252 (Part 1) test report from a recognised lab. You do not wait for a factory inspection the way ISI Scheme I works. The registration number and the BIS Standard Mark go on the product, packaging or rating plate before you stock or sell.

Listed laboratory charges for IS 13252 (Part 1) run ₹25,000–₹1,95,000 excluding GST. Keep the BOM, enclosure, PSU and critical insulation identical to the tested sample — a board spin or adapter swap is a new model and a new CRS line.

If the listed test price looks expensive, contact Certko — we regularly secure up to 30% lesser pricing on USB External Hard Disk Drives / SSDs CRS testing and handle the portal filing so the factory can keep building.

title: Importing USB External Hard Disk Drives / SSDs from Vietnam: CRS registration
heading: Importing USB External Hard Disk Drives / SSDs from Vietnam: CRS registration
excerpt: Vietnam-built USB External Hard Disk Drives / SSDs still needs Indian CRS on IS 13252 (Part 1) before it can be sold here — CR or ASEAN marks are not enough.
body: A growing share of USB External Hard Disk Drives / SSDs now ships from Vietnam instead of China. MIC / CR marks and an ASEAN CB route help other markets. They do not replace BIS CRS for India. The standard remains IS 13252 (Part 1), HSN 84717020. Mandatory (CRS Registration).

Treat the Vietnamese plant as a foreign manufacturer: appoint an AIR if the brand owner sits outside India, test the Vietnam-built sample (not a leftover China unit), and register that construction. A China CRS line does not cover a Vietnam second source unless the BOM and layout are proven identical and BIS accepts the series.

Listed testing for this SKU is ₹25,000–₹1,95,000. If you dual-source China and Vietnam, budget two sample sets and say so on the portal — mixed constructions are the usual query that stalls USB External Hard Disk Drives / SSDs registrations.
Certko files the Vietnam plant as its own manufacturing location on CRS and keeps the China line separate so neither factory blocks the other.

title: Assemble USB External Hard Disk Drives / SSDs in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
heading: Assemble USB External Hard Disk Drives / SSDs in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
excerpt: Importing spare parts or CKD/SKD kits and assembling USB External Hard Disk Drives / SSDs in India does not dodge BIS. You can always take the CRS route on the finished unit.
body: If you import spare parts, SKD or CKD kits of USB External Hard Disk Drives / SSDs from China or Vietnam and want to assemble in India, you can always go for the CRS route. BIS looks at the finished product you place on the Indian market — USB External Hard Disk Drives / SSDs under IS 13252 (Part 1) — not at each screw and bare PCB in the inbound carton.

Unpopulated housings, displays, batteries shipped as parts, or a CKD kit billed as components usually stay outside CRS at the border. The moment your Indian line assembles a complete, usable USB External Hard Disk Drives / SSDs (HSN 84717020 as a finished good), CRS registration is what lets you manufacture and sell it. That is often cleaner than importing a CBU and fighting a finished-goods hold.

Register the Indian assembly site as the manufacturer. Test the unit that actually comes off the Indian line — not a golden sample from Shenzhen — against IS 13252 (Part 1). Lab window 6–10 weeks, listed charges ₹25,000–₹1,95,000. Keep a parts-trace file so a Vietnam substitute cell or adapter does not silently break the registered construction.

Create the BIS CRS login, add the brand and manufacturing address (Indian plant or foreign plant plus AIR), list every model that shares the construction, and upload labels, user manual and a critical-component list. Then send samples to a lab whose scope includes IS 13252 (Part 1).

heading: CRS licence to manufacture Solar PV Modules in India

title: Importing Solar PV Modules from Vietnam: CRS registration
heading: Importing Solar PV Modules from Vietnam: CRS registration
excerpt: Vietnam-built Solar PV Modules still needs Indian CRS on IS 14286 / IS 61730 before it can be sold here — CR or ASEAN marks are not enough.

title: Assemble Solar PV Modules in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
heading: Assemble Solar PV Modules in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
excerpt: Importing spare parts or CKD/SKD kits and assembling Solar PV Modules in India does not dodge BIS. You can always take the CRS route on the finished unit.
body: If you import spare parts, SKD or CKD kits of Solar PV Modules from China or Vietnam and want to assemble in India, you can always go for the CRS route. BIS looks at the finished product you place on the Indian market — Solar PV Modules under IS 14286 / IS 61730 — not at each screw and bare PCB in the inbound carton.

Unpopulated housings, displays, batteries shipped as parts, or a CKD kit billed as components usually stay outside CRS at the border. The moment your Indian line assembles a complete, usable Solar PV Modules (HSN 85414300 as a finished good), CRS registration is what lets you manufacture and sell it. That is often cleaner than importing a CBU and fighting a finished-goods hold.

Register the Indian assembly site as the manufacturer. Test the unit that actually comes off the Indian line — not a golden sample from Shenzhen — against IS 14286 / IS 61730. Lab window 6–10 weeks, listed charges ₹7,00,000–₹12,80,550. Keep a parts-trace file so a Vietnam substitute cell or adapter does not silently break the registered construction.

heading: Importing Electronic Games (Video) from Vietnam: CRS registration
excerpt: Vietnam-built Electronic Games (Video) still needs Indian CRS on IS/IEC 62368-1:2023 before it can be sold here — CR or ASEAN marks are not enough.

title: Assemble Electronic Games (Video) in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
heading: Assemble Electronic Games (Video) in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
excerpt: Importing spare parts or CKD/SKD kits and assembling Electronic Games (Video) in India does not dodge BIS. You can always take the CRS route on the finished unit.
body: If you import spare parts, SKD or CKD kits of Electronic Games (Video) from China or Vietnam and want to assemble in India, you can always go for the CRS route. BIS looks at the finished product you place on the Indian market — Electronic Games (Video) under IS/IEC 62368-1:2023 — not at each screw and bare PCB in the inbound carton.

Unpopulated housings, displays, batteries shipped as parts, or a CKD kit billed as components usually stay outside CRS at the border. The moment your Indian line assembles a complete, usable Electronic Games (Video) (HSN 95045000 as a finished good), CRS registration is what lets you manufacture and sell it. That is often cleaner than importing a CBU and fighting a finished-goods hold.

Register the Indian assembly site as the manufacturer. Test the unit that actually comes off the Indian line — not a golden sample from Shenzhen — against IS/IEC 62368-1:2023. Lab window 6–10 weeks, listed charges ₹5,000–₹6,50,000. Keep a parts-trace file so a Vietnam substitute cell or adapter does not silently break the registered construction.

title: Assemble Smart Card Readers in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
heading: Assemble Smart Card Readers in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
excerpt: Importing spare parts or CKD/SKD kits and assembling Smart Card Readers in India does not dodge BIS. You can always take the CRS route on the finished unit.
body: If you import spare parts, SKD or CKD kits of Smart Card Readers from China or Vietnam and want to assemble in India, you can always go for the CRS route. BIS looks at the finished product you place on the Indian market — Smart Card Readers under IS/IEC 62368-1:2023 — not at each screw and bare PCB in the inbound carton.

Unpopulated housings, displays, batteries shipped as parts, or a CKD kit billed as components usually stay outside CRS at the border. The moment your Indian line assembles a complete, usable Smart Card Readers (HSN 84719000 as a finished good), CRS registration is what lets you manufacture and sell it. That is often cleaner than importing a CBU and fighting a finished-goods hold.

Register the Indian assembly site as the manufacturer. Test the unit that actually comes off the Indian line — not a golden sample from Shenzhen — against IS/IEC 62368-1:2023. Lab window 6–10 weeks, listed charges ₹5,000–₹6,50,000. Keep a parts-trace file so a Vietnam substitute cell or adapter does not silently break the registered construction.

excerpt: Step-by-step CRS filing for Mail Processing / Postage / Franking Machines: portal, samples, IS/IEC 62368-1:2023 report and marking.
body: CRS for Mail Processing / Postage / Franking Machines is a portal filing backed by a IS/IEC 62368-1:2023 test report. Mandatory (CRS Registration). HSN 84729010. You do not book a BIS factory audit for this scheme.

Create the BIS CRS login, add the brand and manufacturing address (Indian plant or foreign plant plus AIR), list every model that shares the construction, and upload labels, user manual and a critical-component list. Then send samples to a lab whose scope includes IS/IEC 62368-1:2023.
Expect 6–10 weeks once samples are in the lab, plus query time. Listed test charges ₹5,000–₹6,50,000. Do not print the Standard Mark until the number is issued.

title: Foreign factory and AIR duties for Mail Processing / Postage / Franking Machines
heading: Foreign factory and AIR duties for Mail Processing / Postage / Franking Machines

Name the actual manufacturing address in China, Vietnam or elsewhere. A trading office is not a factory. If you later assemble the same Mail Processing / Postage / Franking Machines in India, add the Indian site as its own manufacturer — do not hide a second plant behind the AIR.

title: CKD, SKD or CBU for Mail Processing / Postage / Franking Machines — CRS still applies
heading: CKD, SKD or CBU for Mail Processing / Postage / Franking Machines — CRS still applies
excerpt: Knocked-down kits of Mail Processing / Postage / Franking Machines do not skip BIS. Choose the import form, then register the finished goods on CRS.
body: Brands argue CBU versus CKD to cut duty on Mail Processing / Postage / Franking Machines. That is a customs conversation. The compliance conversation is simpler: whatever form you import, the finished Mail Processing / Postage / Franking Machines sold in India needs CRS on IS/IEC 62368-1:2023 (HSN 84729010).

CBU: register before you sell, and usually before you promise a delivery date, because a finished electronic good is easy for customs to query. CKD/SKD: import parts, assemble in India, and take the CRS manufacturer route on the Indian-built unit. Spare parts sold as parts stay out of CRS until they become a complete Mail Processing / Postage / Franking Machines.
You can always go for the assembly-plus-CRS route when the commercial plan is Indian value-add. Test the unit that leaves the Indian line. 6–10 weeks, listed charges ₹5,000–₹6,50,000.
Certko will tell you which cartons are parts and which are Mail Processing / Postage / Franking Machines before you file the Bill of Entry, then run the CRS filing that matches that choice.

title: CRS licence to manufacture Passport Reader in India
heading: CRS licence to manufacture Passport Reader in India
excerpt: What licence and certification a factory needs before it can manufacture Passport Reader (IS/IEC 62368-1:2023) for sale in India.
body: Passport Reader sits on the BIS Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS / Scheme II) against IS/IEC 62368-1:2023. HSN 84719000. Mandatory (CRS Registration). This is a lab-test registration of the brand and model — not a Scheme I ISI factory licence — and you still need it if the finished goods are made in India.

To manufacture Passport Reader in India you typically hold GST, a factory or Udyam record, and then file CRS on the BIS portal with the IS/IEC 62368-1:2023 test report from a recognised lab. You do not wait for a factory inspection the way ISI Scheme I works. The registration number and the BIS Standard Mark go on the product, packaging or rating plate before you stock or sell.

Listed laboratory charges for IS/IEC 62368-1:2023 run ₹5,000–₹6,50,000 excluding GST. Keep the BOM, enclosure, PSU and critical insulation identical to the tested sample — a board spin or adapter swap is a new model and a new CRS line.
If the listed test price looks expensive, contact Certko — we regularly secure up to 30% lesser pricing on Passport Reader CRS testing and handle the portal filing so the factory can keep building.

title: Importing Passport Reader from China: CRS registration
heading: Importing Passport Reader from China: CRS registration
excerpt: A finished Passport Reader made in China cannot be sold in India on a CCC mark. Map IS/IEC 62368-1:2023 CRS before the shipment leaves.
body: Chinese factories often already hold CCC, SRRC or a CB report for Passport Reader. None of those marks let you sell the goods in India. For HSN 84719000 the Indian gate is BIS CRS against IS/IEC 62368-1:2023. Mandatory (CRS Registration).

The Chinese manufacturer can own the CRS registration and appoint an Authorised Indian Representative (AIR), or the Indian importer can register the brand it places on the market. Customs officers check the CRS number on Passport Reader consignments — a missing number is a hold, not a “pay later” option.

Plan 6–10 weeks for testing plus portal queries. Listed charges ₹5,000–₹6,50,000. Do not assume a Shenzhen CB report converts automatically — Indian national differences and the current IS/IEC 62368-1:2023 edition still have to match.
Certko maps the China construction to IS/IEC 62368-1:2023, books the lab, and files CRS so the first container is not the test sample.

title: Importing Passport Reader from Vietnam: CRS registration
heading: Importing Passport Reader from Vietnam: CRS registration
excerpt: Vietnam-built Passport Reader still needs Indian CRS on IS/IEC 62368-1:2023 before it can be sold here — CR or ASEAN marks are not enough.
body: A growing share of Passport Reader now ships from Vietnam instead of China. MIC / CR marks and an ASEAN CB route help other markets. They do not replace BIS CRS for India. The standard remains IS/IEC 62368-1:2023, HSN 84719000. Mandatory (CRS Registration).

Treat the Vietnamese plant as a foreign manufacturer: appoint an AIR if the brand owner sits outside India, test the Vietnam-built sample (not a leftover China unit), and register that construction. A China CRS line does not cover a Vietnam second source unless the BOM and layout are proven identical and BIS accepts the series.

Listed testing for this SKU is ₹5,000–₹6,50,000. If you dual-source China and Vietnam, budget two sample sets and say so on the portal — mixed constructions are the usual query that stalls Passport Reader registrations.
Certko files the Vietnam plant as its own manufacturing location on CRS and keeps the China line separate so neither factory blocks the other.

title: Assemble Passport Reader in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
heading: Assemble Passport Reader in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
excerpt: Importing spare parts or CKD/SKD kits and assembling Passport Reader in India does not dodge BIS. You can always take the CRS route on the finished unit.
body: If you import spare parts, SKD or CKD kits of Passport Reader from China or Vietnam and want to assemble in India, you can always go for the CRS route. BIS looks at the finished product you place on the Indian market — Passport Reader under IS/IEC 62368-1:2023 — not at each screw and bare PCB in the inbound carton.

Unpopulated housings, displays, batteries shipped as parts, or a CKD kit billed as components usually stay outside CRS at the border. The moment your Indian line assembles a complete, usable Passport Reader (HSN 84719000 as a finished good), CRS registration is what lets you manufacture and sell it. That is often cleaner than importing a CBU and fighting a finished-goods hold.

Register the Indian assembly site as the manufacturer. Test the unit that actually comes off the Indian line — not a golden sample from Shenzhen — against IS/IEC 62368-1:2023. Lab window 6–10 weeks, listed charges ₹5,000–₹6,50,000. Keep a parts-trace file so a Vietnam substitute cell or adapter does not silently break the registered construction.

title: Importing Cash Registers from Vietnam: CRS registration

title: Assemble Cash Registers in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
heading: Assemble Cash Registers in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
excerpt: Importing spare parts or CKD/SKD kits and assembling Cash Registers in India does not dodge BIS. You can always take the CRS route on the finished unit.
body: If you import spare parts, SKD or CKD kits of Cash Registers from China or Vietnam and want to assemble in India, you can always go for the CRS route. BIS looks at the finished product you place on the Indian market — Cash Registers under IS/IEC 62368-1:2023 — not at each screw and bare PCB in the inbound carton.

Unpopulated housings, displays, batteries shipped as parts, or a CKD kit billed as components usually stay outside CRS at the border. The moment your Indian line assembles a complete, usable Cash Registers (HSN 84705010 as a finished good), CRS registration is what lets you manufacture and sell it. That is often cleaner than importing a CBU and fighting a finished-goods hold.

Register the Indian assembly site as the manufacturer. Test the unit that actually comes off the Indian line — not a golden sample from Shenzhen — against IS/IEC 62368-1:2023. Lab window 6–10 weeks, listed charges ₹5,000–₹6,50,000. Keep a parts-trace file so a Vietnam substitute cell or adapter does not silently break the registered construction.

title: CRS licence to manufacture Automatic Teller / Cash Dispensing Machines (ATM) in India
heading: CRS licence to manufacture Automatic Teller / Cash Dispensing Machines (ATM) in India
excerpt: What licence and certification a factory needs before it can manufacture Automatic Teller / Cash Dispensing Machines (ATM) (IS/IEC 62368-1:2023) for sale in India.
body: Automatic Teller / Cash Dispensing Machines (ATM) sits on the BIS Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS / Scheme II) against IS/IEC 62368-1:2023. HSN 84729030. Mandatory (CRS Registration). This is a lab-test registration of the brand and model — not a Scheme I ISI factory licence — and you still need it if the finished goods are made in India.

To manufacture Automatic Teller / Cash Dispensing Machines (ATM) in India you typically hold GST, a factory or Udyam record, and then file CRS on the BIS portal with the IS/IEC 62368-1:2023 test report from a recognised lab. You do not wait for a factory inspection the way ISI Scheme I works. The registration number and the BIS Standard Mark go on the product, packaging or rating plate before you stock or sell.

Listed laboratory charges for IS/IEC 62368-1:2023 run ₹5,000–₹6,50,000 excluding GST. Keep the BOM, enclosure, PSU and critical insulation identical to the tested sample — a board spin or adapter swap is a new model and a new CRS line.

If the listed test price looks expensive, contact Certko — we regularly secure up to 30% lesser pricing on Automatic Teller / Cash Dispensing Machines (ATM) CRS testing and handle the portal filing so the factory can keep building.

title: CRS licence to manufacture Induction Stove in India
heading: CRS licence to manufacture Induction Stove in India
excerpt: What licence and certification a factory needs before it can manufacture Induction Stove (IS 302 (Part 2/Sec 6)) for sale in India.
body: Induction Stove sits on the BIS Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS / Scheme II) against IS 302 (Part 2/Sec 6). HSN 85166000. Mandatory (CRS Registration). This is a lab-test registration of the brand and model — not a Scheme I ISI factory licence — and you still need it if the finished goods are made in India.

To manufacture Induction Stove in India you typically hold GST, a factory or Udyam record, and then file CRS on the BIS portal with the IS 302 (Part 2/Sec 6) test report from a recognised lab. You do not wait for a factory inspection the way ISI Scheme I works. The registration number and the BIS Standard Mark go on the product, packaging or rating plate before you stock or sell.

Listed laboratory charges for IS 302 (Part 2/Sec 6) run ₹6,000–₹1,50,000 excluding GST. Keep the BOM, enclosure, PSU and critical insulation identical to the tested sample — a board spin or adapter swap is a new model and a new CRS line.
If the listed test price looks expensive, contact Certko — we regularly secure up to 30% lesser pricing on Induction Stove CRS testing and handle the portal filing so the factory can keep building.

title: Importing Induction Stove from Vietnam: CRS registration
heading: Importing Induction Stove from Vietnam: CRS registration
excerpt: Vietnam-built Induction Stove still needs Indian CRS on IS 302 (Part 2/Sec 6) before it can be sold here — CR or ASEAN marks are not enough.

title: Assemble Induction Stove in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
heading: Assemble Induction Stove in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
excerpt: Importing spare parts or CKD/SKD kits and assembling Induction Stove in India does not dodge BIS. You can always take the CRS route on the finished unit.
body: If you import spare parts, SKD or CKD kits of Induction Stove from China or Vietnam and want to assemble in India, you can always go for the CRS route. BIS looks at the finished product you place on the Indian market — Induction Stove under IS 302 (Part 2/Sec 6) — not at each screw and bare PCB in the inbound carton.

Unpopulated housings, displays, batteries shipped as parts, or a CKD kit billed as components usually stay outside CRS at the border. The moment your Indian line assembles a complete, usable Induction Stove (HSN 85166000 as a finished good), CRS registration is what lets you manufacture and sell it. That is often cleaner than importing a CBU and fighting a finished-goods hold.

Register the Indian assembly site as the manufacturer. Test the unit that actually comes off the Indian line — not a golden sample from Shenzhen — against IS 302 (Part 2/Sec 6). Lab window 6–10 weeks, listed charges ₹6,000–₹1,50,000. Keep a parts-trace file so a Vietnam substitute cell or adapter does not silently break the registered construction.

title: Assemble Rice Cooker in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
heading: Assemble Rice Cooker in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
excerpt: Importing spare parts or CKD/SKD kits and assembling Rice Cooker in India does not dodge BIS. You can always take the CRS route on the finished unit.
body: If you import spare parts, SKD or CKD kits of Rice Cooker from China or Vietnam and want to assemble in India, you can always go for the CRS route. BIS looks at the finished product you place on the Indian market — Rice Cooker under IS 302 (Part 2/Sec 15) — not at each screw and bare PCB in the inbound carton.

Unpopulated housings, displays, batteries shipped as parts, or a CKD kit billed as components usually stay outside CRS at the border. The moment your Indian line assembles a complete, usable Rice Cooker (HSN 85167100 as a finished good), CRS registration is what lets you manufacture and sell it. That is often cleaner than importing a CBU and fighting a finished-goods hold.

Register the Indian assembly site as the manufacturer. Test the unit that actually comes off the Indian line — not a golden sample from Shenzhen — against IS 302 (Part 2/Sec 15). Lab window 6–10 weeks, listed charges ₹10,000–₹2,95,000. Keep a parts-trace file so a Vietnam substitute cell or adapter does not silently break the registered construction.

title: CKD, SKD or CBU for Rice Cooker — CRS still applies
heading: CKD, SKD or CBU for Rice Cooker — CRS still applies
excerpt: Knocked-down kits of Rice Cooker do not skip BIS. Choose the import form, then register the finished goods on CRS.
body: Brands argue CBU versus CKD to cut duty on Rice Cooker. That is a customs conversation. The compliance conversation is simpler: whatever form you import, the finished Rice Cooker sold in India needs CRS on IS 302 (Part 2/Sec 15) (HSN 85167100).

CBU: register before you sell, and usually before you promise a delivery date, because a finished electronic good is easy for customs to query. CKD/SKD: import parts, assemble in India, and take the CRS manufacturer route on the Indian-built unit. Spare parts sold as parts stay out of CRS until they become a complete Rice Cooker.
You can always go for the assembly-plus-CRS route when the commercial plan is Indian value-add. Test the unit that leaves the Indian line. 6–10 weeks, listed charges ₹10,000–₹2,95,000.
Certko will tell you which cartons are parts and which are Rice Cooker before you file the Bill of Entry, then run the CRS filing that matches that choice.

title: CRS licence to manufacture Wireless Microphone in India
heading: CRS licence to manufacture Wireless Microphone in India
excerpt: What licence and certification a factory needs before it can manufacture Wireless Microphone (IS/IEC 62368-1:2023) for sale in India.
body: Wireless Microphone sits on the BIS Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS / Scheme II) against IS/IEC 62368-1:2023. HSN 85181000. Mandatory (CRS Registration). This is a lab-test registration of the brand and model — not a Scheme I ISI factory licence — and you still need it if the finished goods are made in India.

To manufacture Wireless Microphone in India you typically hold GST, a factory or Udyam record, and then file CRS on the BIS portal with the IS/IEC 62368-1:2023 test report from a recognised lab. You do not wait for a factory inspection the way ISI Scheme I works. The registration number and the BIS Standard Mark go on the product, packaging or rating plate before you stock or sell.

Listed laboratory charges for IS/IEC 62368-1:2023 run ₹5,000–₹6,50,000 excluding GST. Keep the BOM, enclosure, PSU and critical insulation identical to the tested sample — a board spin or adapter swap is a new model and a new CRS line. If the Wireless Microphone SKU carries Wi-Fi, Bluetooth or a cellular radio, stack a WPC ETA / equipment type approval on the same project — CRS never replaces the radio licence.

If the listed test price looks expensive, contact Certko — we regularly secure up to 30% lesser pricing on Wireless Microphone CRS testing and handle the portal filing so the factory can keep building.

title: Assemble Digital Camera in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
heading: Assemble Digital Camera in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
excerpt: Importing spare parts or CKD/SKD kits and assembling Digital Camera in India does not dodge BIS. You can always take the CRS route on the finished unit.
body: If you import spare parts, SKD or CKD kits of Digital Camera from China or Vietnam and want to assemble in India, you can always go for the CRS route. BIS looks at the finished product you place on the Indian market — Digital Camera under IS/IEC 62368-1:2023 — not at each screw and bare PCB in the inbound carton.

Unpopulated housings, displays, batteries shipped as parts, or a CKD kit billed as components usually stay outside CRS at the border. The moment your Indian line assembles a complete, usable Digital Camera (HSN 85258100 as a finished good), CRS registration is what lets you manufacture and sell it. That is often cleaner than importing a CBU and fighting a finished-goods hold.

Treat the Vietnamese plant as a foreign manufacturer: appoint an AIR if the brand owner sits outside India, test the Vietnam-built sample (not a leftover China unit), and register that construction. title: Assemble Video Camera in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
heading: Assemble Video Camera in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
excerpt: Importing spare parts or CKD/SKD kits and assembling Video Camera in India does not dodge BIS. You can always take the CRS route on the finished unit.
body: If you import spare parts, SKD or CKD kits of Video Camera from China or Vietnam and want to assemble in India, you can always go for the CRS route. BIS looks at the finished product you place on the Indian market — Video Camera under IS/IEC 62368-1:2023 — not at each screw and bare PCB in the inbound carton.

Unpopulated housings, displays, batteries shipped as parts, or a CKD kit billed as components usually stay outside CRS at the border. The moment your Indian line assembles a complete, usable Video Camera (HSN 85258900 as a finished good), CRS registration is what lets you manufacture and sell it. That is often cleaner than importing a CBU and fighting a finished-goods hold.

Register the Indian assembly site as the manufacturer. Test the unit that actually comes off the Indian line — not a golden sample from Shenzhen — against IS/IEC 62368-1:2023. Lab window 6–10 weeks, listed charges ₹5,000–₹6,50,000. Keep a parts-trace file so a Vietnam substitute cell or adapter does not silently break the registered construction. If the Video Camera SKU carries Wi-Fi, Bluetooth or a cellular radio, stack a WPC ETA / equipment type approval on the same project — CRS never replaces the radio licence.

heading: CKD, SKD or CBU for Video Camera — CRS still applies

excerpt: Importing spare parts or CKD/SKD kits and assembling Standalone Switch Mode Power Supplies (SMPS, <=48V) in India does not dodge BIS. You can always take the CRS route on the finished unit.

title: Importing Utility-Interconnected PV Inverters (Islanding Prevention) from Vietnam: CRS registration
heading: Importing Utility-Interconnected PV Inverters (Islanding Prevention) from Vietnam: CRS registration
excerpt: Vietnam-built Utility-Interconnected PV Inverters (Islanding Prevention) still needs Indian CRS on IS 16270 before it can be sold here — CR or ASEAN marks are not enough.
body: A growing share of Utility-Interconnected PV Inverters (Islanding Prevention) now ships from Vietnam instead of China. MIC / CR marks and an ASEAN CB route help other markets. They do not replace BIS CRS for India. The standard remains IS 16270, HSN 85044090. Mandatory (CRS Registration).

Certko files the Vietnam plant as its own manufacturing location on CRS and keeps the China line separate so neither factory blocks the other.

title: Assemble Utility-Interconnected PV Inverters (Islanding Prevention) in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
heading: Assemble Utility-Interconnected PV Inverters (Islanding Prevention) in India from China or Vietnam parts — CRS is the route
excerpt: Importing spare parts or CKD/SKD kits and assembling Utility-Interconnected PV Inverters (Islanding Prevention) in India does not dodge BIS. You can always take the CRS route on the finished unit.
body: If you import spare parts, SKD or CKD kits of Utility-Interconnected PV Inverters (Islanding Prevention) from China or Vietnam and want to assemble in India, you can always go for the CRS route. BIS looks at the finished product you place on the Indian market — Utility-Interconnected PV Inverters (Islanding Prevention) under IS 16270 — not at each screw and bare PCB in the inbound carton.

Unpopulated housings, displays, batteries shipped as parts, or a CKD kit billed as components usually stay outside CRS at the border. The moment your Indian line assembles a complete, usable Utility-Interconnected PV Inverters (Islanding Prevention) (HSN 85044090 as a finished good), CRS registration is what lets you manufacture and sell it. That is often cleaner than importing a CBU and fighting a finished-goods hold.

Register the Indian assembly site as the manufacturer. Test the unit that actually comes off the Indian line — not a golden sample from Shenzhen — against IS 16270. Lab window 6–10 weeks, listed charges ₹75,000–₹19,50,000. Keep a parts-trace file so a Vietnam substitute cell or adapter does not silently break the registered construction.

title: CRS licence to manufacture Ortho Phosphoric Acid in India
heading: CRS licence to manufacture Ortho Phosphoric Acid in India
excerpt: What licence and certification a factory needs before it can manufacture Ortho Phosphoric Acid (IS 798:2020) for sale in India.
body: Ortho Phosphoric Acid sits on the BIS Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS / Scheme II) against IS 798:2020. HSN 28092010. Mandatory (CRS Registration). This is a lab-test registration of the brand and model — not a Scheme I ISI factory licence — and you still need it if the finished goods are made in India.

To manufacture Ortho Phosphoric Acid in India you typically hold GST, a factory or Udyam record, and then file CRS on the BIS portal with the IS 798:2020 test report from a recognised lab. You do not wait for a factory inspection the way ISI Scheme I works. The registration number and the BIS Standard Mark go on the product, packaging or rating plate before you stock or sell.

Listed laboratory charges for IS 798:2020 run ₹14,000 excluding GST. Keep the BOM, enclosure, PSU and critical insulation identical to the tested sample — a board spin or adapter swap is a new model and a new CRS line.

If the listed test price looks expensive, contact Certko — we regularly secure up to 30% lesser pricing on Ortho Phosphoric Acid CRS testing and handle the portal filing so the factory can keep building.
